svg.title: Atrial fibrillation decision chart: each of its three harms has its own treatment; stroke risk scored by CHADS2 decides anticoagulation, a fast ventricular rate gets AV-nodal blocking drugs, and lost atrial kick gets rhythm control, with cardioversion now only if onset is under 48 hours or the patient is already anticoagulated, otherwise after 3 weeks of anticoagulation

svg.text: Atrial fibrillation (AF): irregularly irregular, no P waves. Treat EACH of its three harms

svg.text: fibrillatory baseline waves, irregular RR intervals · risk rises after 50

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: look for a reversible cause: hypertension, ischemic or valve disease, alcohol, thyroid, lung disease, sleep apnea

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: PAROXYSMAL stops on its own · PERSISTENT needs drugs or cardioversion · PERMANENT: rate control only
